text:
maria: quick ask — I'm seeing a ~10% tail latency regression on small-batch inference (batch=2, seq=512) for the new runtime image. Can someone capture a short perf trace (nsys + torch.profiler) for a 20-request run so we have op-level breakdown? upload to the perf bucket and ping here :eyes:

josh: I can take this. which docker image / commit + model weights should I use?

maria: image: redwood/runtime:2026-03-10-rc2, commit: serve-1.2, model: gpt-small-6b (local weights at /models/gpt-small-6b). keep input short — 20 requests to mimic the PLG traffic.

lee: heads-up: nsys traces blow up quickly. please run a short capture and prefer nvtx+cuda traces only. avoid system-wide sampling. Example command I use:
```
nsys profile --output /tmp/perf_1853212100 --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=none --export=sqlite 
  --capture-range cudaProfilerApi --force-overwrite -- Python -u -m inference.run --model /models/gpt-small-6b --batch_size 2 --requests 20
```
This keeps the file small-ish but includes kernel timings and NVTX ranges.

anika: and add a tiny torch.profiler run inside the script to get operator-level breakdown for the CPU side. snippet: 
```
with torch.profiler.profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA], record_shapes=True, with_stack=False) as prof:
    model.infer(batch)
    # save minimal events
    prof.key_averages().export_chrome_trace('/tmp/torchprof_trace.json')
```
We only need 1-2 steps captured to correlate with the nsys timeline.

maria: also set these env vars: 
```
PYTORCH_JIT=0
TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=0
NSYS_NVLINK_ENABLE=0
```
and start the server with --log-nvtx to get NVTX ranges.

josh: got it. any sanitization rules before uploading? traces may contain absolute paths / UUIDs.

anika: use the sanitize script: `tools/sanitize_trace.py /tmp/perf_1853212100.sqlite --strip-paths --zero-uuids` — that removes host paths and zeroes alloc ids. put sanitized artifacts in s3://redwood-perf/sanitized/1853212100/

lee: if the sqlite is >200MB zip it (we only need the sqlite + torchprof json). Also add a small README.txt with the exact command lines and envs you used.

josh: running now on a spare A100 node; ETA ~15m. I'll upload sanitized artifacts to the perf bucket and drop the presigned link here.

sre-bot: upload started: s3://redwood-perf/tmp/1853212100/uploading... (mock)

maria: perfect — once uploaded I'll run the flamegraph script and annotate the latency regression. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
